annotations.shape: hand-written bytes (tools/write_raw_fixtures.py holds them as typed literals): multipart/alternative (boundary b1-bad-charset) with two text/plain children that both declare charset=x-no-such-charset -- the first body carries an 0xe9 octet (decodable as windows-1252 after the declared rung fails), the second an 0x81 octet (no strict rung decodes it at all)
annotations.provenance: the bytes are frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS and checked by tests/test_fixtures.py; they are not generator output because a declarative renderer would be encoding the very assumption under test (D11's raw hand-written set)
annotations.phase_numbering: the design document's phases: 0 = the Phase 0 skeleton walker (spans, decode chain, accounted regions, gaps), 1 = the Phase 1 parser (header projection, body views, attachment manifest), 2 = routing and statuses, 3 = threading and time evidence
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the design rules (D2/D3/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: these hand-written bytes carry no spare empty line before a boundary, so the CRLF that terminates a child's last body line is the delimiter's leading CRLF (RFC 2046): each child body span ends before it and the regions tile the message exactly
annotations.expected_gaps: body.decode_fallback_used on part 1.1 (the declared charset is unknown and the ladder falls through to windows-1252) and body.decode_destroyed_bytes on part 1.2 (not even windows-1252 decodes 0x81 strictly, so the last-resort replacement decode is the recorded lossy path, never the normal one)
annotations.not_yet_labelled: views and quoting (none here), statuses (phase 2), thread edges and TimeEvents (phase 3); see labels.undetermined for the one design reading this fixture turns on

value: the design requires a deterministic charset ladder (ground rules, D9/D13) but never names the rungs for an RFC 822 body: this label follows the reading named in Turn 0.2 (declared charset, then strict us-ascii, utf-8, windows-1252, then the recorded replacement decode) and asks the design to name those rungs explicitly, because part 1.2's verdict (windows-1252 as the used charset of a *replacement* decode) is exactly the kind of value a different ladder would render differently
